brief: The Market Ear asks whether tech's selloff has bottomed after the SOX posted two consecutive up days and Asian markets rallied. Goldman Prime data show fundamental long/short momentum exposure collapsing from near 70% at the peak to around 15%, and Asian fundamental managers cut net leverage by 16.9 points to 48%, the 21st percentile of the past year, so positioning has washed out in places. In semis, Callahan calls the stretch one of the most painful he recalls: capex and EPS estimates keep rising and the SOX trades near a 1x discount to its 15-year average, yet investors stay reluctant to re-enter until the market rewards earnings revisions rather than compressing multiples further on 'peak' fears. The S&P 500 ex-AI is retreating from its highs while the Nasdaq 100 bounces off its summer range low. Positioning is not fully clean though: Nasdaq futures length stays elevated into MegaCap earnings, and CTA trend signals have weakened, so a further leg lower could trigger more systematic selling. Bottom line: fundamentals are improving, positioning is messy, and the machines don't care.
